harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic center providing home base and stability throughout
C (IV) - Subdominant creating gentle harmonic lift and movement away from tonic
D (V) - Dominant chord providing tension and resolution back to G
The I-IV-V progression is the foundation of country music harmony
The chorus V-IV-I motion creates a powerful plagal-like resolution characteristic of country and folk

techniques.name: Boom-Chicka Strumming
techniques.description: The classic Johnny Cash 'boom-chicka' country strumming pattern with alternating bass notes on beats 1 and 3, and muted strums on beats 2 and 4

notes: G: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (Open G chord)
C: X-3-2-0-1-0 (Open C chord)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (Open D chord)
Beat 1: Strike bass note (root of chord) with thumb or pick downstroke
Beat 2: Muted 'chicka' strum across treble strings (use palm muting)
Beat 3: Strike alternate bass note (usually the 5th) with thumb or pick
Beat 4: Muted 'chicka' strum across treble strings
sequence: For G chord: bass note on low E string (3rd fret), then chicka, then bass on A string (2nd fret), then chicka
For C chord: bass note on A string (3rd fret), then chicka, then bass on D string (2nd fret), then chicka
For D chord: bass note on D string (open), then chicka, then bass on A string (open), then chicka
Maintain steady 4/4 time at 108 BPM throughout
tips: Keep the 'chicka' strums light and percussive by muting with the palm
The bass notes should be the loudest part of each measure
Practice the bass-chicka pattern on a single chord before adding changes
Use a medium pick for balanced attack on bass and strum
Listen to Luther Perkins' original guitar work for the authentic feel
details.progression: G - C - G - D - G (Boom-Chicka Pattern)

techniques.name: Mariachi Horn Line (Guitar Adaptation)
techniques.description: The iconic trumpet melody from the original recording adapted for guitar using single-note picking on the higher strings

notes: The horn line follows the G major scale ascending and descending
Played on the B and high E strings primarily
Key notes: G(3rd fret E string) - A - B - D pattern
Uses quarter notes and eighth notes to match the trumpet phrasing
The melody outlines the G-C-G-D-G chord progression melodically
sequence: Start on G note (3rd fret, high E string)
Ascend through A (5th fret) to B (7th fret)
Descend back through the scale pattern
Resolve on G root note to match the chord change
Repeat the ascending-descending pattern for each phrase
tips: Use alternate picking for clean execution
Let each note ring clearly - the horn line should sing
Practice slowly to get the phrasing right before adding tempo
This can be played simultaneously with the boom-chicka if playing solo
Use the neck pickup for a warmer, rounder tone to emulate brass
details.progression: Over G - C - G - D - G progression

techniques.name: Alternating Bass Pattern
techniques.description: Root-fifth alternating bass note technique that drives the rhythmic foundation of the boom-chicka pattern

notes: G chord: Alternate between G (3rd fret, low E) and D (open D string)
C chord: Alternate between C (3rd fret, A string) and G (3rd fret, low E)
D chord: Alternate between D (open D string) and A (open A string)
The thumb or pick plays bass notes on beats 1 and 3
sequence: Beat 1: Root bass note of current chord
Beat 3: Fifth of current chord as bass note
tips: Practice the bass note alternation slowly without the strum first
Keep your fretting hand stable while the picking hand alternates
The alternating bass creates the the iconic vocal hook feel
This technique is foundational for all Johnny Cash songs

sections.name: Intro (Horn Line)
sections.description: The iconic mariachi trumpet melody that opens the song, adapted here for guitar single-note picking
notes: The horn melody ascends and descends through the G major scale
Originally played by Mexican-style trumpets arranged by Bill McElhiney
Adapt for guitar by playing the melody on the B and high E strings
Maintain even note values to match the trumpet phrasing

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse section with classic boom-chicka strumming pattern supporting the vocal melody
notes: Alternating bass notes on beats 1 and 3 with muted strums on 2 and 4
Keep the rhythm steady and driving like a train
The vocal melody closely follows the chord tones
Luther Perkins' signature sparse guitar style defines this section

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The famous chorus with the signature hook, using a V-IV-I resolution
sections.progression: D - C - G | D - C - G
notes: The chorus starts on the V chord (D) for harmonic lift
Resolves through IV (C) to I (G) in a strong country cadence
Increase strumming intensity slightly for the chorus
The horn line returns between vocal phrases

sections.name: Instrumental Break
sections.description: Return of the horn melody between verses, providing the song's signature instrumental hook
notes: Identical melody to the intro horn line
Serves as a musical interlude between verse sections
Can be played as single notes or with underlying boom-chicka rhythm
Keep timing precise to match the band arrangement

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Final section with repeated chorus and fade, ending on a strong G major resolution
notes: Repeated chorus progression fading out
Horn melody continues over the boom-chicka rhythm
Gradual reduction in volume for the fade ending
Final resolution to G major tonic

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 Acoustic or similar dreadnought
guitar.pickup: Acoustic preferred; if electric, use bridge single-coil for twangy tone

effects.reverb: Light spring reverb for subtle ambience
effects.other: Slapback delay (100-150ms, single repeat) for authentic 1960s Sun Records-style tone

beginner.focus: Learn the three open chords G, C, and D and the basic boom-chicka strum pattern
steps: Master open G, C, and D chord shapes individually
Learn the basic boom-chicka strum: bass note on 1 and 3, strum on 2 and 4
Play through the entire song at a slow tempo (70 BPM) with chord changes

intermediate.focus: Add the alternating bass pattern and learn the horn melody adapted for guitar
steps: Develop root-fifth alternating bass for each chord
Learn the mariachi horn melody as single-note lines on guitar
Combine the boom-chicka rhythm with cleaner bass alternation
Practice at full tempo (108 BPM) with consistent timing

advanced.focus: Combine the horn melody with rhythm guitar simultaneously for solo performance
steps: Play horn melody over boom-chicka bass pattern simultaneously
Add Travis picking elements to the bass pattern
Develop dynamic control between verse and chorus sections
Achieve authentic Johnny Cash tone and feel

commonMistakes: Strumming too hard on the 'chicka' beats - they should be light and percussive
Losing the alternating bass pattern when adding chord changes
Playing the horn melody too fast or out of time with the rhythm
Neglecting the muted strum quality - it should sound crisp, not ringy
Rushing the tempo - maintain the steady train-like groove
practiceRoutine: Warm up with open G, C, D chord changes for 5 minutes
Practice boom-chicka pattern on G chord alone for 3 minutes
Add chord changes to the boom-chicka pattern slowly
Work on the horn melody separately as single-note lines
Combine rhythm and melody at slow tempo, gradually building to 108 BPM
focusAreas: Clean chord transitions between G, C, and D
metronomeWork: Start boom-chicka pattern at 70 BPM on a single chord
Build gradually to performance tempo of 108 BPM
Practice horn melody at 90 BPM before combining with rhythm
